llm.summary: This is a disclosed local VMware audit and policy helper, but it needs Review because its documented global bypass and fail-open defaults can disable protections across the VMware skill family.

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent: audit logging, policy checks, and sanitization for VMware skills. The concern is proportionality: it is a centralized wrapper for 156+ tools and documents complete policy bypass plus allow-all behavior when rules or dependencies are missing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly says it auto-loads for VMware tool calls and audit/policy requests, but its scope is broad and includes a simple environment-variable bypass for all policy checks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv package vmware-policy and exposes a Bash-backed CLI workflow. The artifact itself contains only markdown and metadata; static scan was clean and no VirusTotal telemetry was supplied.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It writes local audit data under ~/.vmware and inspects environment markers for agent detection, including OPENAI_API_KEY presence. The docs say credential values are not stored, but using a credential-bearing variable is broader than necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill maintains persistent SQLite audit logs with operation parameters/results and rotates them locally. It recommends directory permissions, but exported logs and local files can contain sensitive operational metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this package acting as the central audit and policy layer for VMware skills. Before using it in production, create and protect ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED, secure ~/.vmware/audit.db and exported JSON logs, and avoid relying on it as the only control for high-risk VMware operations.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Agent detection is expected for audit logs and is disclosed, but checking OPENAI_API_KEY as a marker is unnecessary exposure to a credential-bearing environment variable even if values are not logged.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The documented VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 global bypass materially weakens a central policy-enforcement skill and is not scoped to emergency/admin use.
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-loading across VMware skills fits the stated infrastructure role, but the breadth increases blast radius if policy, logging, or sanitization behavior is wrong.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The capabilities reference confirms that VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypasses deny rules and maintenance windows while only logging ok_bypassed; this is a real review concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export is expected for this CLI, but the documentation does not strongly warn that exported logs may reveal operational metadata.
[SQP-2] expected: Optional policy rules are disclosed, but allowing all operations when ~/.vmware/rules.yaml is absent creates a fail-open deployment posture users must understand.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide presents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a simple bypass without strong production safeguards or warnings.
